label: PF Backlog 584
title: EDP-03: Investigate & disposition committed SQLite DBs (control-plane.db, portfolio.db) - fixtures vs live runtime; de-commit runtime data
body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-1292. Source: docs/Product_Forge_Enterprise_Performance_Security_DB_Storage_Roadmap.md. Phase item (see epic). Language rule L1 = Go; must pass scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py.

brief.problem: Runtime SQLite DBs committed to repo, mixing live data with source
brief.why: Reduces compliance risk and repo drift

objective: Investigate committed SQLite DBs (control-plane.db, portfolio.db), classify fixture vs live runtime, and de-commit any runtime data.
acceptance_criteria: Each committed DB dispositioned (fixture or runtime) in inventory
No runtime SQLite DBs committed to git
Explicitly labeled fixtures remain reproducible via seed scripts
approach: Classify consumers, extract seeds, remove DBs from git, add .gitignore.
verification: Fresh clone bootstraps without committed DBs
risks: Removing DBs may break tests that assume committed fixtures
Runtime consumers may have implicit live-data dependency
rollback: Restore DBs from git history commit.
evidence: core/portfolio.py, core/agent_runtime.py, core/delivery.py, core/runtime_freshness.py consume stores

analysis.implementation_strategy: Investigate committed SQLite DBs via git history and consumers (core/portfolio.py, core/agent_runtime.py, core/delivery.py); classify as fixture vs live; convert live data to seed scripts; de-commit runtime DBs via .gitignore; retain fixtures explicitly labeled.
dependency_findings: BLOCKED BY BI-PF-1293 (ADR defines expected DB disposition policy)
BLOCKED BY BI-PF-1294 (inventory classifies each DB's tier)
conflict_findings: core/portfolio.py and portfolio supervisor endpoints may rely on committed DBs at runtime — verify bootstrap path
duplication_findings: EDP-07 (BI-PF-1299) will refactor interfaces — do not overlap; this item only removes committed DBs
No existing de-commit work found in backlog
analysis.rationale: Removes committed runtime data, reducing drift and compliance risk before enterprise storage work.
assumptions: control-plane.db and portfolio.db are the only committed runtime DBs
Seed/fixture mechanism exists or is trivial to add
risks: Removing DBs may break tests that assume committed fixtures
Runtime consumers may have implicit live-data dependency
evidence: core/portfolio.py, core/agent_runtime.py, core/delivery.py, core/runtime_freshness.py consume stores
missing_info: Which consumers treat DBs as fixtures vs live state

missing: Fixture vs live classification for each DB
context_review.reason: Consumers and APIs exist; classification requires investigation and human sign-off.

consolidation_proposal.title: EDP-03: Investigate & disposition committed SQLite DBs (control-plane.db, portfolio.db) - fixtures vs live runtime; de-commit runtime data
consolidation_proposal.body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-1292. Source: docs/Product_Forge_Enterprise_Performance_Security_DB_Storage_Roadmap.md. Phase item (see epic). Language rule L1 = Go; must pass scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py.
acceptance_criteria: Both DBs' schemas and readers/writers are documented (owner, retention, source-of-truth).
Runtime DBs are gitignored; only sanitized fixtures remain if required.
ADR document committed covering storage layers, backends, and data-flow decisions
Develop commit SHA pinned and recorded
The 11 interfaces are declared with explicit optional capabilities (versioning/lock/conditional-write/KMS/signed-URL/multipart).
A conformance suite runs against any adapter (starting with WorkerGrid's store as reference).
No domain module depends on a concrete provider.
private buckets, least-privilege credentials, lifecycle/versioning where required; explicit region/backup/replication capability metadata.
Signed URLs only after authorization, constrained to object/method, short TTL.
Provider config stays inside the adapter; conformance suite passes (wrong-region, versions, delete, restore).
